pollers.note: The distributed poller fleet. Each pool's nodes are polled by the pollers registered to it; a pool with no live poller goes unmonitored.
pollers.unavailable: Poller management is unavailable in skeleton mode.

pool.stripNote: — what ties nodes to pollers. Select one to show only its pollers.
pool.nameHint: Letters, digits, _ and - only, up to 63 characters. Used verbatim as the bus subject name.
pool.descHint: Shown on the pool card and in the node assignment picker.
pool.createNote: Creating a pool starts nothing. Polling begins only once you assign nodes or a folder to it AND move a poller into it — with nodes but no poller, their jobs are published where nothing is listening and are discarded.
pool.renameHint: Renaming moves {{nodes}} node assignment(s) and {{pollers}} poller(s) to the new name, in one step.
pool.renameBlocked: Cannot rename: some pollers serving this pool cannot follow the change.
pool.renameBlockedWhy: These pollers are offline, or their build is older than this feature. Renaming would leave them listening for the old name, so poll-now and discovery would stop reaching them with no error shown. Upgrade or bring them back first.
pool.deleteBlocked: Cannot delete: this pool is still in use.
pool.deleteBlockedWhy: Move them first — nodes and folders from the All nodes right-click menu, pollers from the Pool column on this page.
pool.deleteConfirm: Delete {{pool}}. Nothing references it, so no monitoring stops.

pollers.skewHint: This poller is not on core's version ({{core}}). A remote-site poller is upgraded on its own host.
pollers.selfUpgradeHint: A site updater is deployed beside this poller, so an upgrade of this deployment replaces it too.

empty.title: No pollers yet
empty.sub: Pollers appear here once they connect to the bus and send a heartbeat. Use Register poller for the remote-site setup snippet.

gaps.title: Recent monitoring gaps
gaps.note: Windows when core lost contact with a poller. A poller that stayed up but was cut off backfills its metrics for the window on reconnect; alerts are not backfilled (they resume from now).
gaps.passiveHint: Syslog, traps and flow exports arriving in this window were dropped — unlike polled metrics there is nothing to backfill from. SNMP informs are the exception: the sender retries until acknowledged.

nodes.title: Nodes polled by {{id}}
nodes.note: The working set core has published to this poller — what stops being monitored if it goes away.
nodes.empty: This poller holds no nodes right now.
nodes.offline: This poller is offline, so it holds no working set.
nodes.unknown: This core is a standby, so it does not track poller assignments.

remove.title: Remove poller
remove.confirmText: Remove poller {{id}} from the inventory? If it reconnects it will re-register automatically.

register.title: Register a poller
register.intro: Run a poller container at the remote site; it connects outbound to the central NATS bus. Give it an id and a pool, then download its kit — one archive holding the composition, the certificate and an <env>.env</env> that needs no editing. The fields further down are the manual alternative, for a site that already has <file>docker-compose.poller.yml</file>.
register.issued: Downloaded. The token exists only in that archive — Yagra kept a digest of it.
register.invalidToken: Use letters, digits, dash or underscore only.
register.snippetEmpty: Enter a valid ID, pool and bus URL to generate the snippet.

kit.label: Site kit
kit.hint: The composition, the certificate to pin and a ready .env. Unpack it at the site and bring it up — there is nothing to edit. This also registers the poller, so it may be done before the site exists.

pool.label: Pool
pool.hint: Nodes assigned to this pool are polled here.

busUrl.label: Bus URL
busUrl.hint: Include the poller credentials; a TLS URL is required off-site.

caFile.label: CA file path (optional)
caFile.hint: Only when the bus cert is signed by a private CA.

anchor.title: Anchor node for {{id}}
anchor.none: Work it out from the poller's own addresses
anchor.hint: The derived dependency graph takes its direction from how far each node is from a poller, so core needs to know where this poller sits. It normally works that out from the addresses the poller reports — but a poller in a container reports a container-network address that matches no monitored node, and then it has to be named here. Until every pool that has nodes has a placed poller, the derived graph cannot drive alert suppression.

err.anchor: failed to set the anchor node

bus.title: Remote pollers
bus.note: Job messages carry the credentials Yagra uses to reach your devices, so the bus is encrypted and authenticated before a poller at another site may connect to it.

state.internalNote: the bus stays on this host; only the poller running here can reach it.
state.encryptedNote: pollers at other sites can connect over TLS with the certificate below.

bus.noSwitch: The component that turns this on is not deployed or is switched off, so the switch is unavailable. The certificate below is still the one a site must pin.
bus.outage: The bus, this server and the poller running here are all restarted, so monitoring stops for about a minute. A maintenance window is opened for you, and this page will disconnect while it happens.
bus.siteHint: At the site, put the certificate in a file, point <c>YAGRA_BUS_CA_FILE</c> at it, and use the bus URL from the dialog. The address the site dials must be one of the names below.

names.label: Addresses remote pollers will dial
names.hint: Hostnames or IP addresses, separated by commas. A site cannot connect unless the exact address it dials is listed.
names.required: Give at least one address, or no site will be able to connect.

cert.absent: No certificate yet. One is generated automatically the next time this deployment starts.
cert.uncovered: Not covered by this certificate: {{names}}. Reissue it before those sites can connect.

warn.unreadable: The private key cannot be read — the encryption key has changed or been lost. Reissue the certificate, then give the new one to every site.
warn.expired: This certificate has expired. Remote pollers are already refusing to connect. Reissue it, then give the new one to every site.
warn.not_materialized: A newer certificate is stored than the bus is serving. It takes effect the next time the bus restarts.
warn.expiring: This certificate expires soon. Reissuing it means giving the new one to every site, so plan for it rather than waiting.

reissue.title: Reissue the bus certificate
reissue.intro: Generates a new certificate covering the addresses below, plus this host’s internal names.
reissue.afterward: The new certificate is stored at once, but the bus keeps serving the old one until it restarts — and every site has to be given the new file before it can reconnect.
reissue.failed: failed to reissue the bus certificate

enable.title: Accept remote pollers
enable.intro: Encrypts the bus, requires a password on it, and publishes its port. A poller at another site can then connect with the certificate and the secret shown afterwards.

disable.title: Stop accepting remote pollers
disable.intro: Returns the bus to this host only. Every poller at another site stops connecting, and the nodes assigned to it stop being monitored.

handoff.title: Give this to the site
handoff.intro: The site needs both of these. Copy them now.
handoff.onceOnly: Shown once. It is not stored anywhere it can be read again.
handoff.restarting: The bus is being reconfigured now. This page will reconnect on its own once it comes back.

token.title: Bus token — {{id}}
token.sharedHint: This poller is admitted by the deployment-wide bootstrap secret, the same one every other poller without its own token uses.
token.introShared: Issue this poller a token of its own. It downloads an archive holding the site`s .env, the bus certificate, the composition and a short README — everything the machine at the site needs.
token.introOwn: This poller already has its own token. Issuing a new one downloads a fresh archive and invalidates the current one.
token.reissueWarning: The site stops connecting the moment you do this, and starts again once it is running the new archive.
token.downloaded: Downloaded. The token is only in that file — it cannot be shown again.

host.label: Address this site will dial
host.hint: Leave empty to use the address on the bus certificate. It must be one the certificate covers, or the site cannot connect.

selfUpgrade.label: Let this site upgrade with the deployment
selfUpgrade.hint: Adds a second container at the site that holds its Docker socket, so pressing Upgrade here replaces this poller too. Without it the site stays on whatever version it last pulled and is listed as left behind. The site can change this later in its own .env — that file is the one an upgrade never replaces.

move.title: Move {{id}}
move.cellHint: Drag onto a pool above, or use Move.
move.cannot: This poller cannot be moved yet — it is offline, or its build is older than this feature. Upgrade it first.
move.destHint: It starts polling that pool right away. Nothing at the site has to be touched, and nothing restarts. It is serving {{pool}} now.
move.emptyWarn: This is the last poller serving {{pool}}.
move.takeNodesWhy_one: Monitoring continues. {{count}} node moves to {{pool}} as well.
move.takeNodesWhy_other: Monitoring continues. {{count}} nodes move to {{pool}} as well.
move.leaveNodesWhy_one: {{count}} node stops being monitored, and no alert will be raised for it, until a poller serves that pool again.
move.leaveNodesWhy_other: {{count}} nodes stop being monitored, and no alerts will be raised for them, until a poller serves that pool again.

health.note: Yagra's own health: the poll loop, its backing services, fleet data coverage, and host resources.

supportBundle.title: Take a bundle
supportBundle.help: One archive of this deployment's build provenance, health, configuration, database state and core's own logs — for diagnosing a site nobody can open a shell on.
supportBundle.contents: Everything inside is JSON or plain text, MANIFEST.json lists what is carried and what is deliberately left out, and a redaction scan aborts the export rather than releasing a secret. Read it before sending it anywhere.
supportBundle.nodeHelp: Pick a node to also carry its interfaces, what it collects, which metrics are arriving, and its alerts.
supportBundle.err: The support bundle could not be produced.
supportBundle.signInHint: Sign in with a system-management role to take a support bundle.

settings.note: System-wide monitoring defaults. Per-profile overrides take precedence over these.
settings.signInHint: Sign in with a config-management role to change this.

polling.title: Polling
polling.intervalHelp: How often each node is polled, unless its Device profile sets its own interval. {{min}}–{{max}} seconds.

err.range: Enter a whole number of seconds between {{min}} and {{max}}.

neighbors.title: Discovery walks
neighbors.note: What Yagra asks SNMP devices about the network around them, so the map and the dependency graph can be derived instead of typed in. All read-only: Yagra never configures a device.
neighbors.intervalHelp: How often each device is asked — currently {{cadence}}.

neighbors.name: Neighbors (CDP / LLDP)
neighbors.help: Which of this fleet's ports face which devices, with a history of when that changed. Turning this off stops the walks; everything already recorded is kept.

l3.name: Interface addresses
l3.help: Which IP prefixes each device has a foot in. This is what lets the network map derive links from shared subnets rather than from hand-entered parents.

arp.name: ARP / IPv6 neighbor cache
arp.help: Which hosts each router has actually spoken to — the only source that can name a device nobody has added yet. Off by default: this reads a table sized by the network rather than by the device, so it is the one walk that costs a busy switch measurable work. Results appear under Nodes ▸ Discovery.

routing.name: Routing adjacency (OSPF / BGP / routes)
routing.help: Which devices are peered or directly routed to each other — the links that share no subnet, such as a point-to-point /32, an unnumbered OSPF link, or an eBGP session. The routing table is never walked: it is asked about one destination at a time.

media.name: Interface media type
media.help: Which physical medium each Ethernet port runs — 1000BASE-T for copper, 1000BASE-SX or -LX for fibre — shown in the Media column of a node's Interfaces tab. Read once an hour from the device's MAU table, falling back to the transceiver's own part number. Many devices do not report it at all; on those the column stays empty whether this is on or off.

err.range: Enter a whole number of seconds between {{min}} and {{max}}.
err.rangeFor: {{walk}}: enter a whole number of seconds between {{min}} and {{max}}.
err.save: failed to save discovery walk settings

retention.title: Data retention
retention.note: How long each store keeps what. Lowering a window deletes data older than it on the next sweep. Two rows are set by a store's own start flag and cannot be changed from here.
retention.storeUnknown: Unknown — the store did not report a retention flag

err.range: {{name}}: enter a whole number between {{min}} and {{max}}.

integrations.note: Connect external systems monitored through a vendor cloud API.
integrations.unavailable: Integrations are unavailable in skeleton mode (no store).

meraki.desc: Read-only Dashboard API monitoring — availability, uplinks, and traffic across your Meraki organizations.

netbox.desc: Read-only import of your NetBox site hierarchy — Regions and Sites become the folder tree, with map pins.

polling.title: Meraki polling
polling.hint: Global safeguard — instantly halt all Meraki Dashboard API polling fleet-wide, without deleting any organization config.

orgs.title: Organizations
orgs.empty: No Meraki organizations yet. Add one to start monitoring.

addOrg.title: Add Meraki organization
addOrg.apiKeyHint: Use a read-only Dashboard API key. It is sealed (encrypted at rest) and never shown again. Yagra only ever issues read-only GET calls to Meraki.
addOrg.selectHint: Select the organizations to monitor. All share this one API key.
addOrg.noOrgs: This key can't access any organizations.

networks.title: Network scope — {{name}}
networks.hint: Only monitored networks are collected. Un-checking a network stops narrowing API calls to it (existing device nodes are untouched — remove them to stop monitoring a device).
networks.empty: No networks yet — run “Import devices” to enumerate the org first.

cadence.title: Cadence — {{name}}
cadence.rateBudgetHint: Conservative — kept well under the org API cap so the customer keeps headroom.

delete.title: Delete organization
delete.confirmText: Delete {{name}}? Its imported device nodes, network scope, and HostTree groups are removed. Metric history in the TSDB is left. This cannot be undone.

import.title: Import devices — {{name}}
import.allImported: No new devices to import — every device this key can see is already monitored.

err.discover: failed to reach the Meraki API

bundle.pageNote: Move a monitoring configuration from one deployment to another. Admin only, in both directions.
bundle.notBackup: This is not a backup. A bundle carries no credentials, no notification-channel settings, no ingest tokens and no history — for disaster recovery take a database dump (see DEPLOYMENT.md, "Backup & restore").

export.title: Export
export.help: Download this deployment’s configuration as a single JSON file. Built-in profiles, metric sets and rules are left out — the target seeds its own.
export.err: Could not export the configuration bundle.

import.title: Import
import.help: Apply a bundle exported from another deployment. Rows with the same id are updated and new ones created; nothing is ever deleted.
import.warning: Applying this overwrites configuration that shares an id with a row in the bundle. Run the check first: it performs the real import and rolls it back, so the report is exactly what applying would do.

err.invalid-json: That file is not valid JSON.
err.not-a-bundle: That file is not a Yagra configuration bundle.
err.version: This bundle was written by a newer Yagra (bundle version {{version}}). Upgrade this deployment first.
err.failed: The import failed. Nothing was changed.

report.dryRun: Dry run — nothing was saved. Applying would create {{created}}, update {{updated}} and skip {{skipped}}.
report.noop: Nothing to do — this deployment already matches the bundle.

notes.skipped_builtin: Built-in rows were left out — the target seeds its own copies
notes.skipped_missing_reference: Skipped: something the row requires is not on this deployment
notes.reference_dropped: Imported, but a reference this deployment does not have was cleared
notes.secret_dropped_imported_disabled: A secret cannot be carried between deployments, so this arrives disabled unless one is already stored here — re-enter it, then enable
notes.webhook_token_reset: A webhook ingest token cannot be carried, so the source arrives disabled with an unusable token — rotate it to get a working one
notes.schedule_next_run_recomputed: The next run was recomputed from the cadence on this clock

netbox.name: NetBox
netbox.note: Read-only import of the site hierarchy from NetBox. Yagra never writes to NetBox.

servers.title: NetBox deployments
servers.empty: No NetBox deployment is configured. Add one to build the folder tree from its Regions and Sites.
servers.ownership: A sync owns each folder’s name, parent and map position. The poller pool you set on a folder is yours and is never overwritten, and a Site removed in NetBox is flagged here rather than deleted.

form.name: Name
form.baseUrlHint: Including the port if it is not the default, e.g. http://netbox.example.com:8000. Loopback and link-local addresses are refused; private addresses are fine.
form.tokenHint: Stored encrypted. It is never shown again and never returned by the API.
form.tokenKeepHint: Leave empty to keep the stored token.
form.caCertHint: Paste the PEM certificate of the private CA that signed this NetBox. Only this connection trusts it. Never paste a private key.
form.siteIdFieldHint: Which NetBox field holds your site code. It is put in front of the Site's folder name, e.g. “JPMYJ01 Matsuyama Home”. Custom fields defined in this NetBox are listed here.
form.siteIdFieldKeyHint: The custom field's name in NetBox — its key, not its label. Letters, digits and underscores.
form.siteIdFieldKeyInvalid: A custom field name can only contain letters, digits and underscores.
form.siteIdFieldUnreadable: This token cannot read this NetBox's custom field definitions, so they are not listed. Choose “Other” and type the field's name to use one.

siteIdField.none: Do not add a Site ID

test.unreachable: Nothing at that address answered as a NetBox API. Check the URL and the port.
test.badToken: NetBox answered, but refused the token. Check the API token.

siteId.none: No Site ID on any of the {{sites}} sites — check the Site ID field
siteId.partial: {{without}} of {{sites}} sites have no Site ID

delete.title: Remove NetBox deployment
delete.body: Remove “{{name}}”? The folders it created are kept and become ordinary folders — no node loses its place.

err.save: Could not save the NetBox deployment
err.delete: Could not remove the NetBox deployment
